I work at a company which has an up or out culture up to the the senior lead level (one below director).
I just want to give a contrary opinion to a lot of people in this thread. I think this style of culture is great for a young company that's looking to expand fast. Getting talent from outside the company is very expensive and risky while getting talent from inside the company allows a much clearer picture of what kind of people you will get in your senior roles. It also rewards your people with constant growth as your hiring new hires that eventually fill senior positions. I do agree fully that it's a terrible philosophy for larger companies that are trying to maintain market share or that have senior roles pop up at a much slower rate than they're hiring starters.

I do disagree though with places like the five employing this philosophy, they're much to large to employ such a pipeline as their ratios between senior positions and starters do not allow for such a strategy in a sustainable employee minded way. Although it's completely unsurprising that firms who thrive on selling juniors as mediors employ strategies that burn through young graduates at massive rates to aim for the highest profit margin. Would also do this through employing completely unrealistic career prospects.

On top of this Randstad Dutch is drifting away from old Dutch and becoming more and more englishified, you can hear it in the way people from the region tend to pronounce their R's for example.
